title: prune_reopened_refs judges a gone item file against the integration main, not the checkout it runs in
goal: Found by the fresh-context review of SP-matmvkn6, item ST-ihtjygip (Sprint close and drop delete the refs/kb-reopened ref of each item they remove): refs/kb-reopened/* is shared by every worktree of a clone, but prune_reopened_refs judges an item file gone by the checkout the command runs in, so a drop outside a sprint run in an older worktree deletes the reopen ref of a live item filed on main after that worktree branched. The prune deletes a ref only when the item file is absent from the integration main tree too (origin/main), and a ref of an item that exists there is kept.
notes: Merged from ST-6cp6uvmv “A planted test proves close and drop prune the reopen refs of removed items and keep those of live items” at the 2026-10-10 backlog triage: No test names prune_reopened_refs or kb-reopened (grep of _tools: only bl_land.py and bl_items.py). It is the test half of the same function whose fix is ST-vblulwrc, and both carry the same `-k reopened_refs` check, so one item does fix plus planted test. Its goal: Found by the fresh-context review of SP-matmvkn6, item ST-ihtjygip (Sprint close and drop delete the refs/kb-reopened ref of each item they remove): no test names kb-reopened or prune_reopened_refs, so removing the call in cmd_close (_tools/bl_land.py) or cmd_drop (_tools/bl_items.py) passes every gate; ST-ihtjygip's check read only the clone's ref state, which the worker pruned by calling the function by hand. One planted-failure test in _tools/test_land_e2e.py, within the ceiling in _tools/tests_ceiling.json, runs close or drop in an isolated git repo and asserts a removed item's ref is gone, a live item's ref kept, and a drop inside a sprint prunes nothing.
